item.title: Ukraine-built 290 g receiver turns Russian drone signals into live video
item.description: D·Vision SDR scans from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz, covering the band Russia's Molniya drones moved to in June. Experts warn a Russian shift to digital video could sideline it.

item.title: Bulgaria elects Iliana Iotova as its first woman president
item.description: The Central Election Commission confirmed her win over Gyurov in the November 1 runoff, with all 15 members voting in favour.

item.title: British and French troops in Ukraine could fire back if attacked, officials say
item.description: The stabilisation force would count more than 10,000 members, run without US technology, including Starlink, and stay away from the front line. No ceasefire is in force yet.

item.title: Let the Sejm's judges sit
item.description: Karol Nawrocki has refused for seven months to swear in four judges elected by Poland's parliament. When one office stalls a constitutional court, Europe is right to say the answer is a working court, not a standoff.

item.title: Ban addictive design EU-wide, not country by country
item.description: Brussels has the evidence, the findings and the law to stop infinite scroll and autoplay. It must decide now, because a patchwork of national bans leaves you unprotected in Lisbon or Tallinn.
